body:
Playing sports is one of the most common hobbies, but people also love to watch live sports games. If you go to any sports stadium, you will be able to find fans cheering wildly, crying with joy. In the case of football, some famous matches are accompanied by (A)[extreme / moderate] fans, whose overly aggressive support of their team sometimes leads to confrontations with fans from opposition teams. If someone’s joy, sadness, and even anger emerge from the love of their team, what makes them so (B)[devoted / apathetic]? What does it mean for an individual to be a sports fan? And would their passion and cheering actually influence the performance of their team? These questions can be addressed from both an evolutionary and a social psychological perspective.

From an evolutionary perspective, sports fandom emerged from our tribal hunter-gatherer ancestors tens of thousands of years ago. At that time, a person was far more likely to (C)[fail / survive] as a member of a group than as an isolated individual. People could help each other in groups when dealing with difficult tasks, such as carrying hunted animals that were too heavy for one person to handle. This mutual cooperation built trust and fostered relationships among group members. In fact, group membership was so important that tribes with a stronger sense of community were more likely to defeat tribes whose members were less closely allied. Because of this, community membership was a survival mechanism for our ancestors, and the instinct to find one’s own tribe or group has been passed down to modern people. This may be how community membership influences our choice of a sports team and our sense of loyalty to that team.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: (A) extreme — (B) devoted — (C) fail
(A) extreme — (B) apathetic — (C) survive
(A) extreme — (B) devoted — (C) survive
(A) moderate — (B) apathetic — (C) fail
(A) moderate — (B) devoted — (C) survive
solution:
1. (A) 지나치게 공격적인 응원으로 상대 팀 팬과 충돌하기도 한다는 설명이 이어지므로 ‘극단적인(extreme)’ 팬이다.
2. (B) 기쁨·슬픔·분노까지 팀에 대한 사랑에서 나온다면 무엇이 그들을 그토록 ‘열성적으로(devoted)’ 만드는지 묻는 흐름이다.
3. (C) 무거운 사냥감을 함께 옮기는 등 집단에서 서로 도울 수 있었으므로, 고립된 개인보다 집단의 일원일 때 ‘살아남을(survive)’ 가능성이 훨씬 컸다.
4. 따라서 답은 ③이다.

it may be human nature to form a group and ⓐ[feel

Another explanation for sports fandom is a
phenomenon called “basking in reflected glory.” This
means that you feel successful by associating
yourself with others’ success, especially when you
are ⓐconnected to them in some way. This
phenomenon is closely related to people’s love for
their sports teams. People feel ⓑproud when their
team wins the game or performs well. Even though
a team’s triumph may not offer its fans any
ⓒimmediate benefits, the mere act of watching the
game brings them satisfaction. This connection with
sports teams can sometimes grow so ⓓstrong
among some passionate supporters that they even
identify themselves with their teams. Because of this
identification, they often consider criticism toward
their team as a personal attack and become
ⓔobedient in extreme cases.

However, as long as the behavior of sports fans
does not go too far and (A)[benefit / harm] others,
cheering can become a means for them to express
their emotions. Supporting a team passionately can
help people forget about their daily life challenges.
It can also have (B)[positive / negative] effects on
our brains. For instance, when you cheer for a team
and your team wins the game, your brain may
release dopamine. Dopamine, a chemical known as
the “happy hormone,” makes you feel pleasure

particular (C)[thrill / panic] when a team achieves
victory following a series of back-to-back losses.
While you are cheering, your brain may also release
oxytocin, a hormone that contributes to feelings of
bonding between people.

There are also two social psychological theories
that might explain ⓐwhy we cheer for a sports
team: optimal distinctiveness and basking in
reflected glory. Though it may be human nature
ⓑto form a group and feel a sense of belonging
to that group, being a fan of a sports team is
different from just having friends. Optimal
distinctiveness theory states that everyone ⓒhas a
need for inclusion and differentiation. That is,
individuals want ⓓto be included somewhere, but
they also want to be different and unique. These
two basic but competing needs can be satisfied
through group membership. Sports team supporters
are one such group. For example, if you are a fan
of a football team based in your city, you can
satisfy your need for inclusion by supporting the
same team with other in-group members. This can
also make you feel ⓔunique because your team’s
fans are different from the fans of other teams. This
feeling of uniqueness is reinforced by sports teams’
deliberate use of their team colors and songs.

body:
In the past, being a fan of a Korean pop idol typically meant waving colored balloons at concerts and sending gifts. Most fans, often teenagers, admired their idols from a distance. However, over the past three decades, the K-pop fandom culture has evolved dramatically with the development of digital technology. Today, fans actively engage themselves in communication with their idols through social media platforms. They can provide feedback and suggestions, which can have a beneficial influence on their idols. When they see some positive changes in their idols, they feel rewarded for their contribution. In other words, fans have changed from consumers to active participants in the K-pop phenomenon. In addition to this change in their attitudes and roles, today’s fans express their affection in different ways. Instead of showering their idols with material gifts, they organize fundraising and volunteer activities in the name of their idols. For example, fans of a popular idol group have raised funds to support children’s charities. Fans’ efforts not only promote good images of their idols but also foster the value of sharing. This change in fandom culture shows how fans’ interaction with K-pop idols has become more dynamic and meaningful. The new culture brings fans closer to their idols and provides a more inclusive and rewarding experience for them.

emerged from our tribal hunter-gatherer ancestors
tens of thousands of years ago. At that time, a
person was ⓐfar more likely to survive as a

People could help each other in groups when
dealing with difficult tasks, such as carrying hunted
animals that ⓑwere too heavy for one person to
handle. This mutual cooperation built trust and
fostered relationships among group members. In
fact, group membership was so important ⓒwhat
tribes with a stronger sense of community were
likely to defeat tribes whose members were less
closely allied. Because of this, community
membership was a survival mechanism for our
ancestors, and the instinct to find one’s own tribe
or group ⓓhas been passed down to modern
people. This may be ⓔhow community membership

crowds. This means that cheering helps the team’s
performance to some extent, although it may not
be the determining factor.

A notable example of blue carbon can be found
in tidal flats ⓐlocated around the ocean. Research
ⓑconducting in 2021 has revealed that getbol in
Korea stores approximately 13 million tons of
carbon and absorbs over 260,000 tons of carbon
dioxide each year. This means that getbol alone can
(A)offset the carbon dioxide emissions produced by
110,000 cars in a year. Considering that getbol
contains numerous organisms and marine animals
ⓒthat store carbon, the treasure house of blue
carbon has become a (B)promising and sustainable
solution to the current environmental problem.
Scientists worldwide are continuing to explore the
(C)capabilities of tidal flats with the goal of having
them officially ⓓrecognized as blue carbon.
Efforts to Protect Getbol
Getbol in Korea was once considered useless
muddy land, so much of it ⓔhas been reclaimed
for farming and urbanization. This has led to a
decline in the area of tidal flats, ⓕcaused a loss of
biodiversity. To prevent further damage to the marine
ecosystem, both the government and environmental
organizations have been making efforts to protect
the tidal flats by (D)deregulating unnecessary
development. ⓖHad it not been for further efforts
to restore getbol, we would fail to (E)conserve this
valuable ecosystem for future generations.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
solution: ⓑ conducting → conducted (동사구 has revealed에 대한 주 어 Research를 수식하는 분사구를 이루는 분사가 쓰일 수 있 으나, 수식받는 명사 Research가 ‘행해진’ 대상이며 뒤에 이어 진 목적어가 없으므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 conducting 을 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 conducted로 고친다.) ⓕ caused → causing (완전한 절(This ~ flats) 뒤에 접속사 없이 동 사(구)가 연결될 수 없으므로 흐름상 앞 절의 결과를 나타내는 분사구 문을 이끄는 분사 형태가 되어야 하며, 원인에 해당하는 앞 절의 내용 이 ‘초래한’ 주체이고 뒤에 목적어로 명사구 a loss of biodiversity가 있으므로, caused를 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 causing으로 고친다.) ⓖ Had it not been for → Were it not for[If it were not for] 또는 Without[But for] (주절에 ‘조동사 과거형+동사원형’인 would fail이 쓰였으며 흐름상 과거 사실이 아닌 현재 사실과 반 대되는 일을 가정하고 있으므로, ‘~이 없다면, …할 것이다’를 뜻 하는 가정법 과거 표현인 ‘Were it not for[If it were not for/But for/Without] ~, 주어+조동사 과거형+동사원형 …’을 써야 한다. 따라서 과거 사실의 반대를 가정하는 가정법 과거완료 표현인 ‘Had it not been for[If it had not been for/Without/But for] ~, 주어+조동사 과거형+have+p.p. …(~가 없었다면, …했을 것이다)’ 의 Had it not been for를 Were it not for, If it were not for, But for, Without 중 하나로 고친다.)

This is why the international community has been
ⓐ[seeking / sought] solutions to the climate crisis.
In 2015, 195 countries signed the Paris Agreement
to limit the temperature increase to 1.5°C above
pre-industrial levels. The countries agreed upon the
fact ⓑ[that / what] the increase in atmospheric
carbon is a major reason for climate change. One
key strategy to combat it is to achieve “carbon
neutrality,” which ⓒ[involve / involves] maintaining a
balance between the amount of carbon emitted and
carbon absorbed.
The Earth’s Atmosphere Is Like a Bathtub
Let’s imagine that the Earth’s atmosphere is a
large bathtub, and the greenhouse gases emitted
into the atmosphere are like water flowing from a
tap into the bathtub. At the bottom of the bathtub,
there’s a drain that lets the water out. If we keep
the tap running, the water level in the bathtub will
rise, just as greenhouse gas emissions have led to
an increase in atmospheric carbon. This rise in
carbon levels has already resulted in negative
environmental consequences, such as climate
change. To make matters worse, if the water is not
effectively drained, the bathtub will overflow. In
other words, if we don't reduce carbon emissions
sufficiently, atmospheric carbon will continue to
accumulate.

communication today. Did you know that the
seemingly innocent act of looking through emails or
checking your inbox has an environmental impact?

energy-consuming network, contributing to climate
change on our planet. Storing countless email
messages in data centers creates carbon emissions.
These data centers rely on huge servers to store
and access data at all times. Because the centers
use electricity to run the servers and to cool down
the large amounts of heat that they generate, they
consume a significant amount of fossil fuels. Mike
Berners-Lee, the British researcher and author of
How Bad Are Bananas?: The Carbon Footprint of
Everything, looked at our average email traffic. For
example, a short phone-to-phone email has a
carbon footprint of 0.2g of CO₂ emissions. But, a
long email, which takes about ten minutes to write
and three minutes to read on a computer, has a

help to __________________________________________.

다음 글의 시사점으로 알맞은 것은?

One of the most promising ways to reduce carbon
in the atmosphere is to use the “good” carbon on
Earth. The Earth’s carbon can be divided into three
types: black carbon, green carbon, and blue carbon.
Black carbon is released while burning fossil fuels,
such as coal, oil, and gas. It causes the greenhouse
effect, leading to global warming and climate
change. Green carbon, on the other hand, is carbon
absorbed by and stored in land ecosystems, such as
rainforests like the Amazon in South America. It
plays a vital role in maintaining the ecosystem
because it absorbs carbon dioxide through
photosynthesis. Finally, blue carbon is the carbon
stored in the ocean, including coastal and marine
ecosystems such as mangrove wetlands, seagrass
beds, and tidal marshes. The carbon absorption rate
of marine ecosystems is about 50 times faster than
that of land ecosystems. Blue carbon can store up
to 10 times more carbon per unit area than forests
on land, making it highly cost-effective.

Black carbon must be converted into blue carbonto increase the overall rate of photosynthesis.

Land ecosystems are more cost-effective thanmarine ecosystems in absorbing carbon dioxide.
Mangrove wetlands and tidal marshes absorbcarbon at a slower rate than rainforests like theAmazon.

Email is one of the most widely ⓐused forms of
communication today. Did you know that the
seemingly innocent act of looking through emails or
ⓑchecking your inbox has an environmental impact? In reality, email travels through an
energy-consuming network, ⓒcontributing to climate
change on our planet. Storing countless email
messages in data centers ⓓcreate carbon emissions.
These data centers rely on huge servers to store
and access data at all times. Because the centers
use electricity to run the servers and to cool down
the large amounts of heat ⓔthat they generate,
they consume a significant amount of fossil fuels.
Mike Berners-Lee, the British researcher and author
of How Bad Are Bananas?: The Carbon Footprint of
Everything, looked at our average email traffic. For
example, a short phone-to-phone email has a
carbon footprint of 0.2g of CO₂ emissions. But, a
long email, which takes about ten minutes to write
and three minutes to read on a computer, has a
footprint of 17g of CO₂ emissions. So, something as
simple as deleting unnecessary email messages can
help to save the Earth.

choices: Checking your inbox or reading messages mightseem harmless, but it actually affects the environment.
Data centers generate carbon emissions becausethey keep innumerable emails stored.
Huge servers require continuous power to keepdata accessible and ready at all times.
Data centers run exclusively on renewable energy tocool down the massive heat produced by servers.
A brief email sent between mobile devices releasesmuch less carbon dioxide than a lengthy emailwritten and read on a computer.

in the atmosphere is to (A)____________________________
________________________. The Earth’s carbon can be
divided into three types: black carbon, green
carbon, and blue carbon. Black carbon is released
while burning fossil fuels, such as coal, oil, and gas.
It causes the greenhouse effect, leading to global
warming and climate change. Green carbon, on the
other hand, is carbon absorbed by and stored in
land ecosystems, such as rainforests like the
Amazon in South America. It plays a vital role in
maintaining the ecosystem because it absorbs
carbon dioxide through photosynthesis. Finally, blue
carbon is the carbon stored in the ocean, including
coastal and marine ecosystems such as mangrove
wetlands, seagrass beds, and tidal marshes. The
carbon absorption rate of marine ecosystems is
about 50 times faster than that of land ecosystems.
Blue carbon can store up to 10 times more carbon
per unit area than forests on land, making it highly
cost-effective.
(B)청색 탄소의 눈에 띄는 예는 대양 주변에 위치한

2021 has revealed that getbol in Korea stores
approximately 13 million tons of carbon and
absorbs over 260,000 tons of carbon dioxide each
year. This means that getbol alone can offset the
carbon dioxide emissions produced by 110,000 cars
in a year. Considering that getbol contains
numerous organisms and marine animals that store
carbon, the treasure house of blue carbon has
become a promising and sustainable solution to the
current environmental problem. Scientists worldwide
are continuing to explore the capabilities of tidal
flats with the goal of having them officially
recognized as blue carbon.

The Earth’s Atmosphere Is Like a Bathtub
Let’s imagine that the Earth’s atmosphere is a
large bathtub, and the greenhouse gases emitted
into the atmosphere are like water flowing from a
tap into the bathtub. At the bottom of the bathtub,
there’s a drain that lets the water out. If we keep
the tap running, the water level in the bathtub will
rise, just as greenhouse gas emissions have led to
an increase in atmospheric carbon. This rise in
carbon levels has already resulted in negative
environmental consequences, such as climate
change. To make matters worse, if the water is not
effectively drained, the bathtub will overflow. In
other words, if we don't reduce carbon emissions
sufficiently, atmospheric carbon will continue to
accumulate.

Email is one of the most widely used forms of
communication today. Did you know that the
seemingly innocent act of looking through emails or
checking your inbox has an environmental impact?
In reality, email travels through an
energy-consuming network, contributing to climate
change on our planet. Storing countless email
messages in data centers creates carbon emissions.
These data centers rely on huge servers to store
and access data at all times. Because the centers
use electricity to run the servers and to cool down
the large amounts of heat that they generate, they
consume a significant amount of fossil fuels. Mike
Berners-Lee, the British researcher and author of
How Bad Are Bananas?: The Carbon Footprint of
Everything, looked at our average email traffic. For
example, a short phone-to-phone email has a
carbon footprint of 0.2g of CO₂ emissions. But, a
long email, which takes about ten minutes to write

footprint of 17g of CO₂ emissions. So, something as

choices: save the Earth
accelerate climate change
expand data center capacity
speed up internet connection
protect personal information online

위 대화의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: I was so into the story
I found the story so tedious
I was so intrigued by the story

solution:
책은 환상적이었다고 했으며, 빈칸에 이어서 소년이 결국 밤새 전체 책을 다 읽었다는 내용이 이어지므로, 자신의 관심사나 흥미를 표현하는 흐름이 되어야 자연스럽다. 따라서 지루함을 표현하는 ② ‘저는 그 이야기가 꽤 지루하다고 생각했어요’는 빈칸에 알맞지 않다.

body:
Hughie is a charming young man who (A)[have / has] achieved everything except making money. He is in love with Laura Merton, the daughter of a retired colonel. Laura loves him sincerely, but the Colonel won’t let them marry until Hughie (B)[has / will have] 10,000 pounds.
One day, Hughie dropped by (C)[seeing / to see] his friend Alan Trevor, a painter. He was adding the finishing touches to a painting of a beggar. In the studio, the beggar himself was standing on a raised platform. He was an old man with a very pitiful face. His clothes were old and worn out.

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: has / has / seeing
have / has / to see
has / will have / to see
have / will have / seeing
has / has / to see
solution:
(A) 선행사 a charming young man을 수식하는 관계사절에서 현재완료로 쓰인 동사구의 조동사 자리로, 주격 관계대명사 뒤의 동사는 선행사에 수일치 시키므로 선행사인 단수명사구 a charming young man에 수일치시킨 단수 조동사 has가 알맞다..
(B) 주절의 시점이 미래를 나타내더라도 시간 부사절에서는 미래의 일을 현재시제로 나타내므로, 시간을 나타내는 접속사 until이 이끄는 부사절의 동사로 현재시제 동사 has가 알맞다.
(C) 완전한 절(Hughie dropped by)에 흐름상 ‘만나기 위해’라는 의미로 이어져야 하므로 목적을 나타내는 부사적 용법의 to부정사 to see가 알맞다. 참고로, drop by(잠깐 들르다)는 ‘자동사+부사’ 구조의 구동사로 뒤에 by의 목적어가 이어지지 않는다.

body:
“Poor old man!” said Hughie. “How unfortunate he looks! But I suppose, for you painters, his face is his fortune?”
“Certainly,” replied Alan, “you wouldn’t want a beggar to look happy, would you?”
“How much does a model get for sitting?” asked Hughie.
“A shilling an hour,” answered Alan.
“And how much do you get for your picture, Alan?” asked Hughie.
“Oh, for this I get two thousand!”
“Pounds?”
“Guineas. Painters, poets, and doctors always get guineas.”
“Well, I think the model should get a fair share of that,” cried Hughie, laughing. He continued, “as they work just as hard as you do.”
“Nonsense, nonsense! Look at the effort it takes to draw and paint and stand in front of the canvas all day! You mustn’t talk. I’m very busy. Keep quiet,” said Alan.

다음 글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: a debate over the proper evaluation and pricing of artists’ paintings
the model’s dissatisfaction with the small amount he receives for posing
Alan’s dissatisfaction with the compensation received by his model
different views on appropriate compensation for an artist and his model
Hughie’s criticism of Alan for demanding excessive payment for his paintings
solution:
늙은 모델이 불행해 보인다고 생각한 Hughie는 모델이 시간당 1실링을 받는 데 비해 화가는 그림 한 점에 2천 기니를 받는다는 사실을 알고 모델도 화가만큼 열심히 일하므로 그에 상응하는 몫을 받아야 한다고 주장하는 반면, Alan은 그림을 그리고 칠하고 캔버스 앞에 서 있다는 것을 강조하며 Hughie에게 말도 하지 말라고 하면서 반박하는 내용이므로, 글의 주제로 ④ ‘화가와 그의 모델에 대한 적절한 보수에 대한 다른 견해’가 알맞다.
오답
① 화가들의 그림에 대한 적절한 평가와 가격 책정에 대한 논쟁
② 자세를 취한 대가로 받는 적은 금액에 대한 모델의 불만
③ 모델이 받는 보수에 대한 Alan의 불만
⑤ 자신의 그림에 지나친 보수를 요구하는 Alan에 대한 Hughie의 비판

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 고르면?
solution:
ⓒ him → himself (흐름상 주어 he가 혼자 생각하는 상황으로 주어 he와 전치사 to의 목적어가 동일한 대상을 가리키므로 목적격 대명사 him을 재귀대명사 himself로 고친다. 참고로 ‘think to oneself’가 ‘마음속으로 생각하다’라는 뜻의 관용적 표현으로 쓰인다.)
ⓓ blushed → blushing (완전한 절(Hughie said goodbye) 다음에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로 이어지므로 동사가 올 수 없고, 흐름상 동시동작을 나타내는 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이다. 의미상 주어 Hughie가 ‘얼굴을 붉히는’ 주체이며 blush가 ‘얼굴을 붉히다’라는 뜻의 자동사로 쓰이므로 blushed를 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 blushing으로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ told의 간접목적어 Alan에 이어진 직접목적어 자리로, 완전한 절(the frame-maker ~ him)을 이끌어 명사절을 이루는 접속사 that은 알맞다.
ⓑ see의 목적어인 간접의문문으로 의문사구(what money) 뒤에서 평서문의 어순이 되도록 ’주어+동사‘의 어순으로 쓰인 he had는 알맞다.
ⓔ 주어 Hughie에 연결된 과거형 동사 spent, received와 A, B, and C의 병렬 구조를 이루는 과거형 동사 had는 알맞다.

That night he walked into the Palette Club at about eleven o’clock and found Alan sitting alone. Hughie asked, “Hey, Alan! Have you got that picture finished?” and Alan replied, “Finished and framed!” Then, Alan continued, “And (A)by the way, that old model you saw is quite devoted to you. ⓐ그는 네가 누구인지, 어디에 사는지, 그리고 네 (미래) 전망은 무엇인지 알고 싶어했어.”
“My dear Alan,” cried Hughie, “I shall probably find him waiting for me when I go home. Poor old man! I wish I could do something for him. I have some old clothes at home ─do you think he would like any of them? His clothes were (B)worn, falling to pieces.”
“But he looks wonderful in them,” said Alan. “What you call worn clothes I call romance. I find them romantic and (C)appealing. However, I’ll tell him about your offer.”
When Hughie commented seriously, “You painters are (D)heartless,” Alan replied, “An artist’s heart is his head. Our job is to show the world as we see it, not to (E)reform it as we know it. Now tell me how Laura is. The old model was quite interested in her.”

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(E)를 아래와 같이 바꾸어 쓸 때 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: (A): incidentally
(B): intact
(C): attractive
(D): unfeeling
(E): improve
solution:
(B) worn은 ‘해진, 닳은’을 뜻하므로, shabby(다 해진) 등으로 바꾸어 쓸 수 있으며, ‘온전한, 손상되지 않은’을 뜻하는 intact와는 바꾸어 쓸 수 없다.
오답
(A) by the way 그런데 = incidentally 그런데
(C) appealing ‘매력적인’ = attractive 매력적인
(D) heartless 무정한 = unfeeling 무정한
(E): reform ~을 개혁하다 = improve ~을 개선하다

“My dear boy,” said Alan, ⓐsmiling, “that old beggar, as you call him, is one of the richest men in Europe. He is Baron Hausberg. He is a great friend of mine, buys all my pictures, and ⓑasks me a month ago to paint him as a beggar.”

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 1개

solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 1개이다.
ⓑ asks → asked (주어인 He에 수일치한 단수 동사 is, buys와 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬 구조를 이루고 있는 것은 알맞으나, 과거를 나타내는 부사구 a month ago(한 달 전에)로 보아 과거에 이루어진 일이므로 asks를 과거시제 동사 asked로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ 주절(said Alan)에 접속사 없이 콤마로 연결된 분사구문의 분사 자리로, 의미상 주어 Alan이 웃는 주체이자 smile은 자동사이므로 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 smiling은 알맞다.
ⓓ 흐름상 that 이하의 명사절이 나에게 떠오르지 않은 진주어가 되므로, 이에 상응하는 주어 자리의 가주어 it은 알맞다.
ⓔ like와 목적어 his name에 이어진 목적격 보어 자리로, like는 ’like+목적어+목적격 보어(~가 …하는 것을 좋아하다)‘의 5형식에서 목적어와 목적격 보어가 수동 관계일 경우 목적격 보어로 과거분사를 취할 수 있으므로, 과거분사 mentioned는 알맞다.

The next morning, when Hughie was having breakfast, an old gentleman visited his house.
(A) On the outside was written, “A wedding present to Hughie Erskine and Laura Merton, from an old beggar,” and inside was a check for 10,000 pounds.

solution: Hughie의 아침 식사 중에, 한 노신사가 그의 집을 방문했다는 주어진 글 다음에, 주어진 글의 an old gentleman을 The man으로 가리켜 그가 자신이 누구인지 밝히고 용건을 말하려고 하자 Hughie가 그의 말을 끊고 남작에게 사과를 전해달라고 말하는 내용의 (B), Then을 사용해 그 노신사가 미소를 지으며 자신의 용건인 남작이 전해 달라고 한 봉투를 건네는 내용으로 Hughie의 사과 이후에 일어난 행동을 묘사하는 (C), (C)에서 언급된 봉투의 겉면에는 간단한 문구가 있었고 안에는 수표가 있었다는 내용의 (A)로 이어지는 것이 자연스럽다.

Throughout history, people have always tried to understand themselves and the world they live in, and these efforts are ⓐreflected in the stories they tell. An interesting example of such stories is the pourquoi tales, which ⓑaims to explain the origins or reasons behind various phenomena. (A) As the French term pourquoi means “why,” these stories explain the mysteries behind certain events. (B) These imaginative stories, often ⓒfeaturing animals or mythical creatures, provide creative explanations for the world around us. (C) According to this story, leopards were originally plain brown like the desert. (D) However, in order not to reveal ⓓthem while hunting animals in the forest, leopards decided to paint spots on their skins. (E) This story explains ⓔthat leopards developed spots as a means of survival.
Pourquoi tales serve several purposes. They engage readers with imaginative stories, teach lessons, and ⓕserves as a means of passing on knowledge to future generations. These stories explore the complexity of the world around us.

윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
Consider the popular pourquoi tale, How the Leopard Got Its Spots.
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘인기 있는 푸르쿠아 이야기인, “표범이 어떻게 반점을 갖게 되었는가”를 생각해 보자.’라는 뜻으로, 흐름상 Consider는 독자의 주의를 특정 사례로 끌어모으기 위해 ‘생각해 보자’라는 뜻으로 쓰였으므로, 상상력 넘치는 푸르쿠아 이야기들은 종종 동물이나 신화적 생물들을 등장시켜 우리 주변의 세계에 대한 창의적인 설명을 제공한다는 일반 진술이 끝나는 문장의 뒤이자, 주어진 문장의 ‘the popular pourquoi tale, How the Leopard Got Its Spots’를 this story로 가리켜 표범들은 원래 사막처럼 평범한 갈색이었다고 설명하는 문장 앞인 (C)에 들어가는 것이 알맞다.

Hughie spent the day with Laura, received a gentle scolding for his actions, and had to ⓔgo home by carriage.

body:
Throughout history, people have always tried to understand themselves and the world they live in, and these efforts are reflected in the stories they tell. An interesting example of such stories is the pourquoi tales, which aim to ______. As the French term pourquoi means “why,” these stories explain the mysteries behind certain events. These imaginative stories, often featuring animals or mythical creatures, provide creative explanations for the world around us. Consider the popular pourquoi tale, How the Leopard Got Its Spots. According to this story, leopards were originally plain brown like the desert. However, in order not to reveal themselves while hunting animals in the forest, leopards decided to paint spots on their skins. This story explains that leopards developed spots as a means of survival.
Pourquoi tales serve several purposes. They engage readers with imaginative stories, teach lessons, and serve as a means of passing on knowledge to future generations. These stories explore the complexity of the world around us.

윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: account for how or why certain things came to be
predict how unfamiliar natural phenomena will develop over time
offer factual explanations for the consequences of various phenomena
preserve accurate historical records of unusual events for later generations
challenge traditional beliefs by revealing the facts behind ancient stories
solution:
프랑스어로 ‘푸르쿠아’가 ‘왜’를 의미하듯이, 푸르쿠아 이야기들은 특정 사건에 감춰진 신비를 설명한다는 내용이 이어지므로, 푸르쿠아 이야기들은 다양한 현상의 기원이나 이유를 설명하는 것을 목표로 한다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ① ‘어떤 것들이 어떻게 또는 왜 생겨나게 되었는지를 설명한다’가 알맞다.
본문변형 빈칸은 원래 ‘explain the origins or reasons behind various phenomena’였음
오답
② 익숙하지 않은 자연 현상이 시간이 지나면서 어떻게 전개될지를 예측하다
③ 다양한 현상의 결과에 대한 사실에 기반을 둔 설명을 제공하다
④ 특이한 사건들에 대한 정확한 역사적 기록을 후세를 위해 보존하다
⑤ 고대 이야기 뒤에 숨겨진 사실을 밝힘으로써 전통적 믿음에 이의를 제기하다

“Poor old man!” said Hughie. “How unfortunate he looks! But I suppose, for you painters, his face is his (A)[fortune / liability]?”
“Certainly,” replied Alan, “you wouldn’t want a beggar to look happy, would you?”
“How much does a model get for sitting?” asked Hughie.
“A shilling an hour,” answered Alan.
“And how much do you get for your picture, Alan?” asked Hughie.
“Oh, for this I get two thousand!”
“Pounds?”
“Guineas. Painters, poets, and doctors always get guineas.”
“Well, I think the model should get an (B)[equitable / inequitable] share of that,” cried Hughie, laughing. He continued, “as they work just as hard as you do.”
“Nonsense, nonsense! Look at the effort it takes to draw and paint and stand in front of the canvas all day! You mustn’t talk. I’m very (C)[idle / busy]. Keep quiet,” said Alan.

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: fortune / equitable / idle
fortune / equitable / busy
liability / inequitable / idle
liability / equitable / busy
fortune / inequitable / busy
solution:
(A) Alan이 당연하다고 대답하며 거지가 행복해 보이는 게 이상한 상황이라는 의미로 ‘거지가 행복해 보이길 바라는 건 아니겠지, 그렇지?’라고 질문하고 있으므로 이에 앞서 Hughie의 질문으로 노인의 참 불행해 보이는 얼굴이 모델로서 유리한 점이 맞냐는 질문이 되는 흐름이 되는 fortune(자산)이 알맞다.
liability 불리한 요소
(B) 모델들도 화가들만큼 열심히 일하기 때문이라는 이유를 덧붙이고 있으므로, 그 모델도 그 돈에서 공정한 몫을 받아야 한다는 흐름이 되는 equitable(공정한)이 알맞다.
inequitable 불공정한
본문변형 a fair → an equitable
(C) Alan은 Hughie의 말을 부정하며 하루 종일 캔버스 앞에서 그리고 서있는 데 드는 노력을 보라고 하면서 자신의 노고를 강조했고 Hughie에게 조용히 하라고 말하고 있으므로 자신이 지금 매우 할 일이 많다는 흐름이 되는 busy(바쁜)가 알맞다.
idle 한가한, 놀고 있는

body:
W: Welcome to Riley’s Science Podcast. Before we start, let’s take a moment to think about our childhood. Personally, I was a kid with a lot of questions. I was curious about everything around me, like why leaves change color in the fall. I also wondered how boats float on water and how flies can walk upside down on the ceiling! Because I asked so many questions, my friends used to laugh at me. But I can say with confidence that my curiosity has made my life more interesting. With a constant desire to learn and explore, I’ve never felt bored. So, if you want to find excitement and joy in your life, I highly recommend staying curious and not being afraid to ask silly questions. Now let’s listen to the stories of people who have achieved great things thanks to their curiosity.
다음 담화의 목적으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: to introduce scientific questions that can be answered through careful observation
to describe how curiosity has influenced the achievements of notable individuals
to explain how curiosity develops throughout childhood and adulthood
to inspire listeners to remain curious to find excitement in their lives
to discuss the relationship between curiosity and success in various fields

Have you ever wondered, “What if I could run so fast that nobody could see me?” If you have asked this kind of question, you may be ready to become the next Galileo. The Italian scientist Galileo Galilei is famous for a thought experiment, which is an imaginary experiment designed to explore a mathematical or scientific hypothesis. With only his thoughts, he demonstrated that objects with different masses should fall at the same speed when dropped from the same height in the absence of air resistance. With a hypothesis based on creativity and imagination, anyone can become a great scientist.
다음 글의 요지로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Understanding the laws of motion is essential for developing accurate scientific hypotheses.
Scientific theories can only be proven through physical experiments rather than imaginary ones.
Scientific progress depends more on advanced experimental techniques than on individual creativity.
Creative imagination and curiosity can lead to meaningful scientific discoveries through thought experiments.
Thought experiments are less reliable than physical experiments because they lack direct observation.
solution: 이 글은 갈릴레오의 사고 실험을 예시로 들어, 창의성과 상상력을 바탕으로 한 사고 실험을 통해 누구나 과학적 가설을 탐구할 수 있다는 내용의 글로, ❹ ‘창의적 상상력과 호기심은 사고 실험을 통해 의미 있는 과학적 발견으로 이어질 수 있다.’가 요지로 적절하다.

body:
The tallest man in recorded history was 272 cm tall, but have you ever wondered what would happen if humans could grow to enormous sizes like the giant in Jack and the Beanstalk? Unfortunately, the answer to this hypothetical question is that it is impossible due to the scale effect. When the length of an object doubles, its area increases by a factor of four (2x2), and its volume by a factor of eight (2x2x2). These changes can create many problems that would put the giant’s life in danger.
다음 글의 요지를 아래와 같이 쓸 때, 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 알맞게 쓰시오. (단, 주어진 철자로 시작할 것)
If the human body became e______, surface area and v______ would increase at d______ rates, potentially creating numerous life-threatening p______.
solution: 정답은 enormous, volume, different, problems 이다. (해설 없음)

body:
One issue is that the giant would not be able to stand properly on his own because of the weight pushing down on his feet. If a person’s height ⓐincreased ten times, his weight would increase by a factor of 1,000 (10x10x10) because weight changes in proportion to volume. However, the area of the feet ⓑsupporting his body would only increase by a factor of 100 (10x10). This means that his feet would be under too much pressure to support the increased weight because the mass ⓒwould have increased far more than the area of his feet.
In addition, there is an issue of heat emission. Heat is generated in the human body, and it is constantly released from the surface of the skin to prevent heat from accumulating in the body. If a person’s height ⓓwere to increase ten times, the amount of heat generated would increase a thousand times in proportion to the body’s volume. However, the surface area of the person’s skin would only increase a hundred times, and as a result, not enough heat would be released from the body through the skin. This shows that while we may wish to grow as ⓔtall as a giant, we would not be able to survive in that form.
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ에 대한 설명으로 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: ⓐ: 현재 사실과 반대되거나 현재에 일어난 가능성이 희박한 상황을 가정하는 가정법 과거가 쓰였다.
ⓑ: 수식받는 the area of the feet이 ‘지탱하는’ 주체이므로 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 supporting이 쓰였다.
ⓒ: 앞 절의 would be보다 먼저 일어난 일(무게 증가)을 나타내기 위해 가정법 과거완료 would have increased가 쓰였다.
ⓓ: 조건절에 쓰이는 be to용법으로, ‘~하고자 한다면’의 의미로 의도를 나타내는 were to increase가 쓰였다.
ⓔ: ‘as+형용사/부사+as’ 형태의 원급 비교이며, 동사 grow의 보어 역할을 하는 형용사 tall이 쓰였다.
solution: ⓓ if절의 ‘were+to부정사‘는 현재 또는 미래에 실현 가능성이 희박한 일을 가정할 때 사용하는 가정법 과거이며, 이때 주어의 인칭과 수에 관계없이 were을 사용하므로 were to increase가 쓰였다.

body:
[1]
“O, swear not by the moon, the inconstant moon.” This is a famous line from Romeo and Juliet. Juliet warns Romeo not ⓐ[swearing / to swear] his love by the Moon as it may change just as the Moon changes its shape. Although its appearance changes, the Moon is always present in the night sky and plays a crucial role in ⓑ[regulation / regulating] the length of the day on Earth as well as the Earth’s seasons and weather patterns. Then, what would happen if there were no Moon?
Without the Moon, our day would no longer be 24 hours. The Moon’s gravity causes the Earth’s ocean to rise and fall. Since the ocean is moving and the Earth is also spinning, friction occurs between them. This friction leads to a decrease in the rotation rate of the planet. Without the Moon, however, the Earth’s rotation would not slow down, resulting in a change in the length of a day. According to some scientists, when the Earth first formed, there was no Moon and a day was only five hours long. This indicates that without the Moon, we would see the Sun rise every five hours.
[2]
Oxygen is a vital gas for life, making up 21 percent of the Earth’s atmosphere. It is essential for breathing and is also necessary to burn common fuels like wood and oil to generate heat and light. Undoubtedly, it is an indispensable element for organisms on Earth. Then, would it be better to have a higher concentration of oxygen in the atmosphere? What would happen if the oxygen concentration were to double?
While more oxygen may seem beneficial, it could have unexpected consequences, especially for insects. Insects, such as bees and dragonflies, do not have lungs and instead take in air through external openings called spiracles. Although insects can survive without lungs, their spiracles are not as ⓒ[efficient / efficiently] as lungs at taking in air.
Therefore, with the current oxygen concentration, insects cannot evolve to be larger than their current size. If they were bigger in size, oxygen would not be able to reach the deepest parts of their bodies. However, if the concentration of oxygen were to double, insects could grow in size as oxygen would be more readily available. This increase in insect size could have a significant influence on the ecological environment, potentially disrupting the food chain. Dragonflies, for example, may become as large as eagles, altering the balance of predators and prey in the ecosystem.
윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
ⓐ / ⓑ / ⓒ
choices: swearing / regulation / efficient
to swear / regulating / efficiently
swearing / regulating / efficient
to swear / regulation / efficiently
to swear / regulating / efficient
solution:
ⓐ 동사 warn은 ‘warn+목적어+목적격보어((not+)to부정사)(~에게 …하(지 말)라고 경고를 주다)’의 5형식 구문으로 쓰이므로 목적격보어로 to부정사 to swear가 알맞다.
ⓑ 전치사 in의 목적어 자리이며 뒤에 명사구 the length를 목적어로 취할 수 있어야 하므로 동명사 regulating이 알맞다.
ⓒ ‘as+형용사/부사+as’ 형태의 원급 비교 구문이 쓰였으며, 동사 are에 이어지는 주격 보어가 as 사이에 쓰여야 하므로 형용사 efficient가 알맞다.

body:
Additionally, the absence of the Moon would completely change weather patterns on Earth. We experience the beauty of different seasons because the Earth is tilted on its axis. The axis of rotation of the Earth is tilted at an angle of 23.5 degrees, and the Moon’s gravity holds the Earth in place by stabilizing the tilt. However, if there were no Moon, the tilt could vary wildly between 0 and 85 degrees. Suppose the Earth were tilted at an angle of 60 degrees. The hemisphere of the Earth facing the Sun would receive much more energy from the sun than the other hemisphere. This could bring about extreme shifts in weather patterns, potentially ______. If this trend continued, the Earth would become uninhabitable.
윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: allowing both hemispheres to receive equal amounts of solar energy
reducing the total amount of solar radiation reaching the Earth
preventing extreme temperature changes across different regions
widening the temperature gap between summer and winter
stabilizing global temperatures near the equatorial regions
solution: 지구가 60도의 각도로 기울어진 상황에서는 태양을 접하고 있는 반구가 다른 반구보다 훨씬 많은 태양 에너지를 받으며, 이것이 기후 패턴에 있어 극단적인 변화를 가져온다고 했으므로 계절에 따른 기온 차이가 더욱 커질 수 있다고 추론할 수 있다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 ❹ ‘여름과 겨울 사이의 기온 차이를 확대시키는’이 적절하다.

2. What if there were no Moon?
“O, swear not by the moon, the inconstant moon.” This is a famous line from Romeo and Juliet. Juliet warns Romeo not to swear his love by the Moon as it may change just as the Moon changes its shape. Although its appearance changes, the Moon is always present in the night sky and plays a crucial role in regulating the length of the day on Earth as well as the Earth’s seasons and weather patterns. Then, what would happen if there were no Moon?
ⓐIf it had not been for the Moon, our day would no longer be 24 hours. The Moon’s gravity causes the Earth’s ocean to rise and fall. Since the ocean is moving and the Earth is also spinning, friction occurs between them. This friction leads to a decrease in the rotation rate of the planet. Without the Moon, however, the Earth’s rotation would not slow down, resulting in a change in the length of a day. According to some scientists, when the Earth first formed, there was no Moon and a day was only five hours long. This indicates that without the Moon, we would see the Sun rise every five hours.
Additionally, the absence of the Moon would completely change weather patterns on Earth. We experience the beauty of different seasons because the Earth is tilted on its axis. The axis of rotation of the Earth is tilted at an angle of 23.5 degrees, and the Moon’s gravity holds the Earth in place by stabilizing the tilt. However, if there were no Moon, the tilt could vary wildly between 0 and 85 degrees. ⓑSupposing the Earth were tilted at an angle of 60 degrees. The hemisphere of the Earth facing the Sun would receive much more energy from the sun than the other hemisphere. This could bring about extreme shifts in weather patterns, potentially making summers hotter and winters colder. If this trend continued, the Earth would become uninhabitable.

M: Suji, you’ve been working on your homework for so long. Aren’t you hungry? How about a snack?
G: A snack sounds great. I want some hot dogs!
M: Okay. I’ll heat up some frozen hot dogs in the microwave.
G: Thank you! It seems like microwaves can cook almost anything. Dad, have you ever wondered how they work? (A)I’m curious about the science of microwaves.
M: Well, it uses radiation to heat food. The radiation causes the water molecules in the food to vibrate and produce heat.
G: Oh, so it’s the moisture in the food that makes the microwave work?
M: Exactly. Without water molecules, the microwave wouldn’t be able to heat the food.
G: Wow, I didn’t know that. So, if I spray some water on the frozen hot dogs, will they heat up faster?

G: Yay! Time for a snack!

오답

body:
The tallest man in recorded history was 272 cm tall, but have you ever wondered what ⓐwould happen if humans could grow to enormous sizes like the giant in Jack and the Beanstalk? Unfortunately, the answer to this hypothetical question is that it is impossible due to the scale effect. When the length of an object doubles, its area increases by a factor of four (2x2), and its volume by a factor of eight (2x2x2). These changes can create many problems ⓑthat would put the giant’s life in danger.
One issue is ⓒwhat the giant would not be able to stand properly on his own because of the weight pushing down on his feet. If a person’s height increased ten times, his weight would increase by a factor of 1,000 (10x10x10) because weight changes in proportion to volume. (A) However, the area of the feet ⓓsupports his body would only increase by a factor of 100 (10x10). (B) This means that his feet would be under too much pressure to support the increased weight because the mass would have increased ⓔfar more than the area of his feet.
In addition, there is an issue of heat emission. Heat is generated in the human body, and it is constantly released from the surface of the skin to prevent heat from accumulating in the body. (C) If a person’s height were to increase ten times, the amount of heat generated would increase a thousand times in proportion to the body’s volume. (D) However, the surface area of the person’s skin would only increase a hundred times, and as a result, not enough heat would be released from the body through the skin. (E)

This shows that while we may wish to grow as tall as a giant, we would not be able to survive in that form.

윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘이것은 우리가 거인만큼 크게 자라기를 바라지만 우리는 그 형태로는 생존할 수 없을 거라는 것을 보여준다.’라는 뜻으로, This(이것)가 가리키는 것이 생존이 불가능한 이유라는 것을 알 수 있다. 글의 흐름상 두 번째 문단은 무게 증가(1000배)에 비해 상대적으로 적은 발의 면적 증가(100배)로 인해 거인이 스스로 똑바로 서있을 수 없음을 설명하고 있으며, 세 번째 문단은 우리 몸에서 발생하는 열의 증가량(1000배)에 비해 표면적의 증가(100배)가 상대적으로 적어에 충분한 열이 배출되지 않는다는 설명을 하고 있다. 따라서 우리 생존과 직결된 것은 열 배출 문제를 설명하는 세 번째 문단이며, This가 가리키는 것은 열 배출과 관련된 결과(결과적으로, 충분한 열이 피부를 통하여 신체로부터 배출되지 않을 것)이므로 이 뒤인 (E)에 들어가는 것이 적절하다.

2. What if there were no Moon?
“O, swear not by the moon, the inconstant moon.” This is a famous line from Romeo and Juliet. Juliet warns Romeo not ⓐto swear his love by the Moon as it may change just as the Moon changes its shape. Although its appearance changes, the Moon is always present in the night sky and plays a crucial role in regulating the length of the day on Earth as well as the Earth’s seasons and weather patterns. Then, what would happen if there ⓑwere no Moon?
Without the Moon, our day would no longer be 24 hours. The Moon’s gravity causes the Earth’s ocean ⓒto rise and fall. Since the ocean is moving and the Earth is also spinning, friction occurs between them. This friction leads to a decrease in the rotation rate of the planet. Without the Moon, however, the Earth’s rotation would not slow down, ⓓresulting in a change in the length of a day. According to some scientists, when the Earth first formed, there was no Moon and a day was only five hours long. This indicates that without the Moon, we would see the Sun ⓔto rise every five hours.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓔ to rise → rise (지각동사 see의 목적격보어 자리로, 지각동사의 목적격보어는 목적어와 목적격보어가 능동 관계일 때 동사원형 또는 진행을 강조하는 현재분사를 쓰고, 목적어와 목적격보어가 수동 관계일 때는 과거분사를 쓴다. 여기서 목적어 the Sun은 ‘뜨는’ 주체이자 rise가 자동사로 쓰였으므로, 목적격보어로 능동을 나타내는 동사원형 rise가 와야 한다. 따라서 to rise를 동사원형 rise로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ 동사 warn은 ‘warn+목적어+목적격보어((not+)to부정사)(~에게 …하(지 말)라고 경고를 주다)’의 5형식 구문으로 쓰이므로 목적격 보어로 쓰인 to부정사 to swear는 적절하다.
ⓑ ‘달이 없다면 무슨 일이 일어날까?‘라는 현재 사실과 반대되는 일(달인 없는 상황)을 가정하고 있으므로 가정법 과거 ‘If+주어+과거 동사 ~, 주어+과거형 조동사+동사원형 …’이 쓰였으며, 이때 If절의 동사로 be동사가 올 때는 주어의 수와 관계없이 과거동사 were을 쓰는 것이 원칙이므로 뒤에 주어 no Moon에 관계없이 were이 쓰인 것은 적절하다.
ⓒ 동사 causes는 ‘cause+목적어+목적격보어(to부정사)’의 5형식 구문으로 쓰이므로 목적격보어 자리의 to부정사 to rise는 적절하다.
ⓓ 완전한 절(the Earth’s ~ down)에 접속사나 주어 없이 콤마(,)로만 연결되므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 의미상 주어인 앞 절 전체가 변화를 ‘가져오는[야기하는]’ 주체이자 result는 자동사이므로, 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 resulting은 적절하다.

Additionally, the absence of the Moon would ______. We experience the beauty of different seasons because the Earth is tilted on its axis. The axis of rotation of the Earth is tilted at an angle of 23.5 degrees, and the Moon’s gravity holds the Earth in place by stabilizing the tilt. However, if there were no Moon, the tilt could vary wildly between 0 and 85 degrees. Suppose the Earth were tilted at an angle of 60 degrees. The hemisphere of the Earth facing the Sun would receive much more energy from the sun than the other hemisphere. This could bring about extreme shifts in weather patterns, potentially making summers hotter and winters colder. If this trend continued, the Earth would become uninhabitable.

윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: stabilize the Earth's rotational axis
completely change weather patterns on Earth
dramatically decrease the Earth’s rotation speed
cause the difference between high and low tides to disappear entirely
reduce the difference in solar energy received by the two hemispheres
solution:
우리가 다른 계절의 아름다움을 경험할 수 있는 이유는 자전축이 23.5도 기울어져 있기 때문이며, 달의 중력이 그 기울기를 안정시키기에 달이 없으면 자전축의 기울기가 크게 변할 것이고, 특히 지구의 기울기가 60도까지 변할 경우 여름은 더 덥고 겨울은 더 추워지는 등 극단적인 날씨 변화가 나타날 수 있다고 했으므로, 달의 부재가 초래할 빈칸에 들어갈 알맞은 말은 ② ‘지구의 기후 패턴을 완전히 바꾸다’가 적절하다.

④ 만조와 간조의 차이를 완전히 사라지게 하다
⑤ 두 반구가 받는 태양 에너지의 차이를 줄이다

Oxygen is a vital gas for life, ⓐ[makes / making] up 21 percent of the Earth’s atmosphere. It is essential for breathing and is also necessary to burn common fuels like wood and oil to generate heat and light. Undoubtedly, it is an indispensable element for organisms on Earth. Then, would it be better ⓑ[have / to have] a higher concentration of oxygen in the atmosphere? What would happen if the oxygen concentration were to double?
(A) Therefore, with the current oxygen concentration, insects cannot evolve to be larger than their current size. If they were bigger in size, oxygen would not be able to reach the deepest parts of their bodies.
(B) However, if the concentration of oxygen were to double, insects could grow in size as oxygen would be more readily available. This increase in insect size could have a significant influence on the ecological environment, potentially disrupting the food chain.
(C) While more oxygen may seem beneficial, it could have unexpected consequences, especially for insects. Insects, such as bees and dragonflies, do not have lungs and instead take in air through external openings called spiracles. Although insects can survive without lungs, their spiracles are not as ⓒ[efficient / efficiently] as lungs at taking in air.
Dragonflies, for example, may become as large as eagles, altering the balance of predators and prey in the ecosystem.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 대기 중에 더 높은 농도의 산소가 있는 것이 더 좋을 것인지, 산소 농도가 두 배가 된다면 무슨 일이 일어나는지 묻는 주어진 글 뒤에, 이 질문에 대한 답변으로 특히 곤충들에게 예상치 못한 결과가 발생할 수 있다고 언급하는 (C)가 이어져야 한다. 곤충은 폐가 없고 외부의 숨구멍을 통해 공기를 받아들이는데, 그 숨구멍이 폐만큼 효율적이지 않다는 (C)에 이어, Therefore(그러므로)로 이어져 현재 산소 농도에서는 곤충이 더 커질 수 없다고 설명한 뒤, 그 이유를 설명하는 (A)가 이어지며, 이후 However(그러나)를 통해 산소 농도가 두 배가 되면 곤충이 산소를 더 쉽게 이용할 수 있어 더 크게 자랄 수 있다는 반대 상황을 제시하는 (B)로 이어지는 흐름이 자연스럽다.

body:
Oxygen is a vital gas for life, ⓐ[makes / making] up 21 percent of the Earth’s atmosphere. It is essential for breathing and is also necessary to burn common fuels like wood and oil to generate heat and light. Undoubtedly, it is an indispensable element for organisms on Earth. Then, would it be better ⓑ[have / to have] a higher concentration of oxygen in the atmosphere? What would happen if the oxygen concentration were to double?
(A) Therefore, with the current oxygen concentration, insects cannot evolve to be larger than their current size. If they were bigger in size, oxygen would not be able to reach the deepest parts of their bodies.
(B) However, if the concentration of oxygen were to double, insects could grow in size as oxygen would be more readily available. This increase in insect size could have a significant influence on the ecological environment, potentially disrupting the food chain.
(C) While more oxygen may seem beneficial, it could have unexpected consequences, especially for insects. Insects, such as bees and dragonflies, do not have lungs and instead take in air through external openings called spiracles. Although insects can survive without lungs, their spiracles are not as ⓒ[efficient / efficiently] as lungs at taking in air.
Dragonflies, for example, may become as large as eagles, altering the balance of predators and prey in the ecosystem.

윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
ⓐ ⓑ ⓒ
choices: making to have efficiently
makes have efficient
making to have efficient
makes to have efficiently
making have efficient
solution:
ⓐ 완전한 절(Oxygen ~ life)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 이어지므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 의미상 주어인 Oxygen이 ‘차지하는’ 주체이므로 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 making이 적절하다.
ⓑ 가주어 it에 상응하는 진주어 자리이므로 to부정사 to have가 적절하다.
ⓒ 'not as+원급(형용사/부사)+as'의 형태로 ‘~만큼 …하지 않은’의 의미를 갖는 원급 비교의 부정형으로, 여기서는 be동사 are에 이어지는 보어 자리이므로 형용사 efficient가 적절하다.

body:
Without the Moon, our day would no longer be 24 hours. The Moon’s gravity causes the Earth’s ocean to rise and fall. Since the ocean is moving and the Earth is also spinning, friction occurs between them. This friction leads to a decrease in the rotation rate of the planet. Without the Moon, however, the Earth’s rotation would not slow down, resulting in a change in the length of a day. According to some scientists, when the Earth first formed, there was no Moon and a day was only five hours long. This indicates that without the Moon, we would see the Sun rise every five hours.
(A)______, the absence of the Moon would completely change weather patterns on Earth. We experience the beauty of different seasons because the Earth is tilted on its axis. The axis of rotation of the Earth is tilted at an angle of 23.5 degrees, and the Moon’s gravity holds the Earth in place by stabilizing the tilt. (B)______, if there were no Moon, the tilt could vary wildly between 0 and 85 degrees. Suppose the Earth were tilted at an angle of 60 degrees. The hemisphere of the Earth facing the Sun would receive much more energy from the sun than the other hemisphere. This could bring about extreme shifts in weather patterns, potentially making summers hotter and winters colder. If this trend continued, the Earth would become uninhabitable.

다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B)
choices: In short But
In other words Therefore
Moreover For instance
Additionally However
That is For example
solution:
(A) 앞에서 달이 없으면 지구의 자전 속도가 느려지지 않아 하루의 길이가 달라진다고 설명한 뒤, 빈칸 뒤에서 달이 없을 때 발생할 또 다른 문제로 날씨 패턴의 변화를 추가로 언급하고 있으므로 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 Moreover(게다가), Additionally(게다가)가 적절하다.
(B) 앞에서 달의 중력이 지구의 자전축 기울기를 안정시킨다고 설명한 뒤, 달이 없을 경우에는 자전축의 기울기가 크게 변할 수 있다는 반대되는 내용을 제시하고 있으므로 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 But, However(그러나)가 적절하다.
오답
① 요약하자면 그러나
② 다시 말해서 따라서
③ 게다가 예를 들어
⑤ 다시 말해서 예를 들어

body:
Have you ever heard the expression “I love you to the moon and back”? This expression conveys a deep extent of love, and uses the great distance between the Earth and the Moon as a metaphor. While this expression is easily understood, there are idioms with a scientific background that may not be so obvious. One example is the phrase “once in a blue moon.” Although people may have seen a magnificent full moon brightening the night sky or a tiny crescent resembling a clipped fingernail, it is highly unlikely that they have seen a blue moon. Surprisingly, this extraordinary event does occur. Normally, there is only one full moon in a month. However, every 2.5 years, there can be two full moons in the same month. The second moon is called a “blue moon,” and it occurs because the Moon completes its cycle of phases in only about 29.5 days. From this rare phenomenon of a blue moon emerged the use of the expression “once in a blue moon.” It describes something that happens exceptionally infrequently.

Some common English expressions have (A)______ origins that are not immediately apparent, as illustrated by the expression “once in a blue moon,” which refers to an extremely (B)______ occurrence.

다음 글을 아래와 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
(A) (B)
choices: scientific rare
scientific frequent
cultural rare
cultural frequent
historical often
solution:
[요약문] 극히 (B)드문 일을 가리키는 표현인 ‘once in a blue moon’에서 볼 수 있듯이, 일부 흔히 사용되는 영어 표현들은 쉽게 알아차리기 어려운 (A)과학적 기원을 가지고 있다.
오답
② 과학적 자주
③ 문화적 드문
④ 문화적 자주
⑤ 역사적 종종

body:
Oxygen is a vital gas for life, making up 21 percent of the Earth’s atmosphere. It is essential for breathing and is also necessary to burn common fuels like wood and oil to generate heat and light. Undoubtedly, it is an indispensable element for organisms on Earth. Then, would it be better to have a higher concentration of oxygen in the atmosphere? What would happen if the oxygen concentration were to double?
While more oxygen may seem beneficial, it could have unexpected consequences, especially for insects. Insects, such as bees and dragonflies, do not have lungs and instead take in air through external openings called spiracles. Although insects can survive without lungs, their spiracles are not as efficient as lungs at taking in air.
Therefore, with the current oxygen concentration, insects cannot evolve to be larger than their current size. If they were bigger in size, oxygen would not be able to reach the deepest parts of their bodies. However, if the concentration of oxygen were to double, insects could (A)[shrink / grow] in size as oxygen would be more readily available. This increase in insect size could have a significant influence on the ecological environment, potentially disrupting the food chain. Dragonflies, for example, may become as large as eagles, (B)[altering / maintaining] the balance of predators and prey in the ecosystem.
Fortunately, you wouldn’t need to worry about giant insects chasing after you if this were to occur. If the oxygen concentration were to double, you would be able to run (C)[slower / faster] than you can right now. Considering that oxygen is used to break down energy so that muscles can use it, the increase in oxygen would help to use energy more efficiently and improve our capability for physical exercise. ㉠이것은 우리에게 운동선수들이 올림픽 경기에서 새로운 세계 기록을 수립하는 것을 기대하게 할 것이다.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: grow altering faster
shrink maintaining faster
grow altering slower
shrink altering faster
grow maintaining slower
solution:
(A) 효율적이지 않은 숨구멍을 가진 곤충들은 크기가 현재보다 더 커지면 산소가 몸의 가장 깊은 부위에 도달할 수 없기에 현재 산소 농도에서는 곤충이 현재보다 더 크게 진화할 수 없다고 설명한 뒤, 산소 농도가 두 배가 되면 산소를 더 쉽게 이용할 수 있다고 했으므로 곤충의 크기가 더 커질 수 있다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 grow(커지다)가 적절하다.
shrink 줄어들다
(B) 곤충의 크기가 증가하면 생태계에 큰 영향을 미쳐 먹이사슬을 교란할 수 있고, 잠자리와 같은 곤충이 독수리만큼 커질 수 있다고 했으므로 포식자와 피식자의 균형을 변화시킨다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 altering(변화시키는)이 적절하다.
maintain ~을 유지하다
(C) 산소가 두 배가 되면 에너지를 더 효율적으로 사용하여 운동 능력이 향상될 수 있다고 설명하고 있으므로 지금보다 더 빨리 달릴 수 있다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 faster(더 빨리)가 적절하다.
slow 느리게

body:
Good evening, everyone. Welcome to the November Book Concert. I’m especially excited to introduce tonight’s author, who is known as the queen of winter. When I read her books, I was fascinated by her descriptions of the winter landscape. (A) They are so vivid and alive that I felt like I was in a world of snowflakes. (B) She has written a number of best-selling novels. (C) Into the Aurora is a story about a young girl who goes on a journey to see the Northern Lights. (D) While enjoying the snow and the stars, they learn about the beauty of nature. (E) Starry Starry Nights has been translated into five languages. We’re honored to have her here tonight to talk about her works. Please join me in welcoming the gifted and inspiring author Alice Lee.
주어진 문장: Another novel, Starry Starry Nights, is about a family that moves to Alaska.
윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘또 다른 소설인 “별이 빛나는 밤”은 알래스카로 이주하는 한 가족에 관한 이야기입니다.’라는 뜻으로, Another(또 다른)로 또 다른 소설을 추가 설명하는 흐름이므로, Alice Lee의 베스트셀러 소설 중 북극광을 보러 여행을 떠나는 어린 소녀의 이야기인 “오로라 속으로”을 설명하는 문장의 뒤이자, they로 주어진 문장의 ‘a family that moves to Alaska(알래스카로 이주하는 한 가족)’를 가리켜 그들이 눈과 별을 즐기면서 자연의 아름다움에 대해 알게 된다며 소설의 내용을 소개하는 문장 앞인 (D)에 들어가는 것이 적절하다.

body:
Hughie is a charming young man who has achieved everything except making money. He is in love with Laura Merton, the daughter of a retired colonel. Laura loves him ⓐsincerely, but the Colonel won’t let them marry until Hughie has 10,000 pounds.
One day, Hughie dropped by to see his friend Alan Trevor, a painter. He was adding the finishing touches to a painting of a beggar. In the studio, the beggar himself was standing on a raised platform. He was an old man with a very ⓑmiserable face. His clothes were old and worn out.
“Poor old man!” said Hughie. “How unfortunate he looks! But I suppose, for you painters, his face is his ⓒasset?”
“Certainly,” replied Alan, “you wouldn’t want a beggar to look happy, would you?”
“How much does a model get for sitting?” asked Hughie.
“A shilling an hour,” answered Alan.
“And how much do you get for your picture, Alan?” asked Hughie.
“Oh, for this I get two thousand!”
“Pounds?”
“Guineas. Painters, poets, and doctors always get guineas.”
“Well, I think the model should get a ⓓreasonable share of that,” cried Hughie, laughing. He continued, “as they work just as hard as you do.”
“ⓔExactly, exactly! Look at the effort it takes to draw and paint and stand in front of the canvas all day! You mustn’t talk. I’m very busy. Keep quiet,” said Alan.
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 흐름상 어색한 것은?
solution: ⓔ Exactly, exactly(바로 그거야, 바로 그거야) → Nonsense, nonsense(말도 안 돼, 말도 안 돼)

body:
That night he walked into the Palette Club at about eleven o’clock and ⓐfinding Alan sitting alone. Hughie asked, “Hey, Alan! Have you got that picture ⓑfinished?” and Alan replied, “Finished and framed!” Then, Alan continued, “And by the way, that old model you saw is quite devoted to you. He wanted to know who ⓒare you, where you live, and what your prospects are.”
“My dear Alan,” cried Hughie, “I shall probably find him waiting for me when I go home. Poor old man! I wish I ⓓcould do something for him. I have some old clothes at home ─do you think he would like any of them? His clothes were worn, ⓔfell to pieces.”
“But he looks wonderful in them,” said Alan. “What you call worn clothes (A)______. I find them romantic and appealing. However, I’ll tell him about your offer.”
When Hughie commented seriously, “You painters are heartless,” Alan replied, “(B)An artist’s heart is his head. Our job is to show the world as we see it, ⓕnot to reform it as we know it. Now tell me how Laura is. The old model was quite interested in her.”

is where I find artistic value

allow us painters to reform the world

After a while, the servant came in and told Alan that the frame-maker wanted to see him. Alan said, “I will be back in a moment,” as he went out. The old beggar took advantage of Alan’s absence to rest for a moment on a chair. He looked so sad and lonely. Hughie couldn’t help pitying him and felt his own pockets to see what money he had. All he could find, however, was a few coins. “Poor old fellow, he wants them more than I do, but it means no carriage for two weeks,” he thought to himself. He walked across the studio and put the coins into the beggar’s hand. The old man was surprised and smiled faintly. “Thank you, sir,” he said. Then Alan arrived, and Hughie said goodbye, blushing a little at what he had done.

On the outside was written, “A wedding present to Hughie Erskine and Laura Merton, from an old beggar,” and inside ⓕwere a check for 10,000 pounds.

body:
Throughout history, people have always tried to understand themselves and the world ⓐ[which / where] they live in, and these efforts are reflected in the stories they tell. An interesting example of such stories is the pourquoi tales, which aim to explain the origins or reasons behind various phenomena. As the French term pourquoi means “why,” these stories explain the mysteries behind certain events. These imaginative stories, often featuring animals or mythical creatures, ⓑ[provide / providing] creative explanations for the world around us. Consider the popular pourquoi tale, How the Leopard Got Its Spots. According to this story, leopards were originally plain brown like the desert. However, in order not to reveal themselves while hunting animals in the forest, leopards decided to paint spots on their skins. This story explains that leopards developed spots as a means of survival.
Pourquoi tales serve several purposes. They engage readers with imaginative stories, ⓒ[teach / teaches] lessons, and serve as a means of passing on knowledge to future generations. These stories explore the complexity of the world around us.
윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
ⓐ      ⓑ      ⓒ
choices: which providing teach
which provide teaches
where provide teach
where providing teaches
which provide teach
solution:
ⓐ 전치사의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(they live in)을 이끌어 선행사인 명사구 the world를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로, 주격 관계대명사 which가 알맞다.
ⓑ 명사구 These imaginative stories와 두 개의 콤마(,)로 삽입되어 명사구를 부연 설명하는 분사구 뒤에 있으며, 뒤에 이어진 다른 동사(구)가 없이 명사구(creative explanations ~)만 이어지므로 문장의 동사 자리이다. 따라서 현재동사 provide가 알맞다.
ⓒ 주어인 복수대명사 They에 수일치한 복수 동사 engage, serve와 함께 ‘A, B, and C’의 구조로 병렬 연결되어 있으므로, 복수 동사 teach가 알맞다.

body:
One day, Hughie dropped by to see his friend Alan Trevor, a painter. He was adding the finishing touches to a painting of a beggar. In the studio, the beggar himself was standing on a raised platform. He was an old man with a very pitiful face. His clothes were old and worn out.
“Poor old man!” said Hughie. “How unfortunate he looks! But I suppose, for you painters, his face is his fortune?”
“Certainly,” replied Alan, “you wouldn’t want a beggar to look happy, would you?”
“How much does a model get for sitting?” asked Hughie.
“A shilling an hour,” answered Alan.
“And how much do you get for your picture, Alan?” asked Hughie.
“Oh, for this I get two thousand!”
“Pounds?”
“Guineas. Painters, poets, and doctors always get guineas.”
“Well, I think the model should get a fair share of that,” cried Hughie, laughing. He continued, “as they work just as hard as you do.”
“Nonsense, nonsense! Look at the effort it takes to draw and paint and stand in front of the canvas all day! You mustn’t talk. I’m very busy. Keep quiet,” said Alan.

Feeling (A)______ for Alan’s poor-looking model and learning about the large difference in their earnings, Hughie argues that the model deserves a fairer share, while Alan emphasizes the (B)______ required of the painter.
(A)      (B)
choices: compassion ease
disgust labor
sympathy exertion
admiration patience
pity idleness
solution: 정답은 ③ 이다. (해설 없음)

body:
That night he walked into the Palette Club at about eleven o’clock and found Alan sitting alone. Hughie asked, “Hey, Alan! Have you got that picture finished?” and Alan replied, “Finished and framed!” Then, Alan continued, “And by the way, that old model you saw is quite devoted to you. He wanted to know who you are, where you live, and what your prospects are.”
“My dear Alan,” cried Hughie, “I shall probably find him waiting for me when I go home. Poor old man! I wish I could do something for him. I have some old clothes at home ─do you think he would like any of them? His clothes were worn, falling to pieces.”
“But he looks wonderful in them,” said Alan. “What you call worn clothes I call romance. I find them romantic and appealing. However, I’ll tell him about your offer.”
When Hughie commented seriously, “You painters are heartless,” Alan replied, “An artist’s heart is his head. Our job is to show the world as we see it, not to reform it as we know it. Now tell me how Laura is. The old model was quite interested in her.”
How does Hughie feel about Alan’s attitude toward the old model’s worn clothes?
choices: He disapproves of Alan’s lack of sympathy for the old man.
He commends Alan for valuing artistic appeal over the model’s hardship.
He objects to Alan’s view that the worn clothes diminish the old man’s appeal as a model.
He feels indifferent to Alan’s opinion because the model‘s appearance does not concern him.
He finds Alan’s artistic response to the model fully understandable from a painter’s perspective.

Hughie is a charming young man who has achieved everything except ⓐ______. He is in love with Laura Merton, the daughter of a retired colonel. Laura loves him sincerely, but the Colonel won’t let them marry until Hughie has 10,000 pounds.
One day, Hughie dropped by to see his friend Alan Trevor, a painter. He was adding the finishing touches to a painting of a beggar. In the studio, ⓑ그 거지 본인이 높은 단상 위에 서 있었다. He was an old man with a very pitiful face. His clothes were old and worn out.

윗글의 빈칸 ⓐ에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?

winning Laura’s affection
attaining financial success
proving his artistic talent to others
receiving his family’s approval for marriage
solution:
모든 것을 이룬 매력적인 젊은 남자인 Hughie가 아직 달성하지 못한 것으로, 대령은 Hughie가 1만 파운드를 벌기 전까지는 결혼을 허락하지 않을 것이라는 내용이 이어지므로, Hughie는 돈을 버는 것을 제외하고 모든 것을 이룬 매력적인 젊은 남자라는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ③ ‘재정적인 성공을 이루는 것’이 알맞다.
본문변형 빈칸은 원래 ‘making money’였음

① 친한 친구를 사귀는 것
② Laura의 사랑을 얻는 것
④ 자신의 예술적 재능을 다른 사람들에게 입증하는 것
⑤ 결혼에 대한 자기 가족의 승낙을 받는 것

body:
“Poor old man!” said Hughie. “How ⓐunfortunately he looks! But I suppose, for you painters, his face is his fortune?”
“Certainly,” replied Alan, “you wouldn’t want a beggar to look happy, ⓑwould you?”
“How much does a model get for sitting?” asked Hughie.
“A shilling an hour,” answered Alan.
“And how much do you get for your picture, Alan?” asked Hughie.
“Oh, for this I get two thousand!”
“Pounds?”
“Guineas. Painters, poets, and doctors always get guineas.”
“Well, I think the model should get a fair share of that,” cried Hughie, ⓒlaughing. He continued, “as they work just as hard as you ⓓare.”
“Nonsense, nonsense! Look at the effort it takes to draw and paint and ⓔstand in front of the canvas all day! You mustn’t talk. I’m very busy. Keep quiet,” said Alan.

윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것을 모두 고르면?
choices: Hughie supposed that the beggar’s miserable appearance might be an advantage to him as a painter’s model.
Alan believed that a beggar serving as a model should appear miserable.
According to Alan, the model’s payment was not fixed.
Alan told Hughie that he would earn a total of two thousand pounds for the painting.
Alan rejected Hughie’s suggestion and stressed the considerable effort involved in producing a painting.
solution:
모델은 시간당 1실링을 받는다고 했으므로, ③ ‘Alan에 따르면, 모델의 보수는 고정된 것이 아니었다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.
Alan은 이 그림으로 2천을 받으며, 파운드가 아닌 기니로 받는다고 했으므로, ④ ‘Alan은 Hughie에게 자신은 그 그림의 대가로 총 2천 파운드를 벌게 될 것이라고 말했다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.
오답
① Hughie는 그 거지의 비참한 외모가 화가의 모델로서 그에게 유리한 점이 될 수 있다고 생각했다.
② Alan은 모델 역할을 하는 거지는 비참해 보여야 한다고 생각했다.
⑤ Alan은 Hughie의 제안을 받아들이지 않았고 그림을 제작하는 데 수반되는 상당한 노력을 강조했다.

That night he walked into the Palette Club at about eleven o’clock and found Alan ⓐsitting alone. Hughie asked, “Hey, Alan! Have you got that picture ⓑto finish?” and Alan replied, “Finished and framed!” Then, Alan continued, “And by the way, that old model you saw is quite devoted to you. He wanted to know who you are, where you live, and what your prospects are.”
(A) When Hughie commented seriously, “You painters are heartless,” Alan replied, “An artist’s heart is his head. Our job is ⓒto show the world as we see it, not to reform it as we know it. Now tell me how ⓓis Laura. The old model was quite interested in her.”
(B) “But he looks wonderful in them,” said Alan. “ⓔThat you call worn clothes I call romance. I find them romantic and appealing. However, I’ll tell him about your offer.”
(C) “My dear Alan,” cried Hughie, “I shall probably find him waiting for me when I go home. Poor old man! I wish I ⓕcould do something for him. I have some old clothes at home ─do you think he would like any of them? His clothes were worn, falling to pieces.”

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 1개
2개
3개
4개
5개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 3개이다.
ⓑ to finish → finished (got의 목적어 that picture에 이어진 목적격 보어 자리로, ‘get+목적어+목적격 보어(~가 …하게 하다)’의 5형식에서 목적어와 목적격 보어가 수동 관계일 때 목적격 보어로 과거분사를 취하며 목적어 that picture가 ‘마무리된’ 대상이므로 to finish를 과거분사 finished로 고친다. 참고로, 목적어와 목적격 보어가 능동 관계일 경우 목적격 보어로 to부정사를 취한다.)
ⓓ is Laura → Laura is (동사 tell의 직접목적어인 간접의문문으로 how 이하는 의문사(how) 뒤 평서문의 어순이 되어야 하므로, is Laura를 ’주어+동사‘의 어순인 Laura is로 고친다.)
ⓔ That → What (’call+목적어+목적격 보어’의 5형식을 이루는 두 번째 동사 call과 목적격 보어인 romance 사이에서 강조를 위해 문장 앞으로 이동하여 목적어를 이루어야 하므로, 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(you call worn clothes)을 이끌어 명사절을 이루도록 That을 ‘~한 것’의 의미로 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사 What으로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ find는 ‘find+목적어+목적격 보어(~가 …하고 있는 것을 발견하다)’의 5형식에 쓰일 때 목적어와 목적격 보어 사이가 능동 관계일 경우 목적격 보어로 현재분사를 취하며, 목적어 Alan이 앉아 있는 주체이며 sit은 자동사이므로 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 sitting은 알맞다.
ⓒ be동사 is의 보어 자리로, ‘보여주는 것’이라는 뜻의 명사적 용법의 to부정사 to show는 알맞다.

public 공적인

These ⓑimaginative stories, often featuring animals or mythical creatures, provide creative explanations for the world around us. Consider the popular pourquoi tale, (A)______. That night he walked into the Palette Club at about eleven o’clock and found Alan sitting alone. Hughie asked, “Hey, Alan! Have you got that picture finished?” and Alan replied, “Finished and framed!” Then, Alan continued, “And by the way, that old model you saw is quite devoted to you. He wanted to know who you are, where you live, and what your prospects are.”
“My dear Alan,” cried Hughie, “I shall probably find him waiting for me when I go home. Poor old man! I wish I could do something for him. I have some old clothes at home ─do you think he would like any of them? His clothes were worn, falling to pieces.”
“But he looks wonderful in them,” said Alan. “What you call worn clothes I call romance. I find them romantic and appealing. However, I’ll tell him about your offer.”
When Hughie commented seriously, “You painters are heartless,” Alan replied, “An artist’s heart is his head. Our job is to show the world as we see it, not to reform it as we know it. Now tell me how Laura is. The old model was quite interested in her.”

윗글의 두 번째 문단에서 네 번째 문단까지의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Hughie’s genuine concern for the old model’s worn clothes
the importance of proper clothing in creating a successful painting
the contrast between Hughie’s compassion and Alan’s artistic perspective
a disagreement over whether poor people should serve as models for artists
Alan’s effort to persuade Hughie to appreciate the artistic value of poverty
solution:
늙은 모델의 낡은 옷을 생각하며 자신의 옷을 주겠다며 연민을 느끼는 Hughie와 그 낡은 옷은 그림의 소재로서 낭만적이고 매력적이라고 생각하며 화가는 세상을 보는 그대로 세상을 보여 주는 거라는 견해를 가진 Alan의 상반된 시각을 보여주므로, 글의 주제로 ③ ‘Hughie의 동정심과 Alan의 예술적 관점 사이의 대조’가 알맞다.
오답
① 늙은 모델의 낡은 옷에 대한 Hughie의 진심 어린 걱정
② 성공적인 그림을 만드는 데 있어 적절한 의상의 중요성
④ 가난한 사람들이 화가의 모델로 일해야 하는지에 대한 의견 차이

body:
Throughout history, people have always tried to understand themselves and the world they live in, and these efforts are reflected in the stories they tell. An interesting example of such stories is the pourquoi tales, which aim to explain the origins or reasons behind various phenomena. As the French term pourquoi means “why,” these stories explain the mysteries behind certain events. These imaginative stories, often featuring animals or mythical creatures, provide creative explanations for the world around us. Consider the popular pourquoi tale, How the Leopard Got Its Spots. According to this story, leopards were originally plain brown like the desert. However, in order not to reveal themselves while hunting animals in the forest, leopards decided to paint spots on their skins. This story explains that leopards developed spots as a means of survival.
Pourquoi tales serve several purposes. They engage readers with imaginative stories, teach lessons, and serve as a means of passing on knowledge to future generations. These stories explore the complexity of the world around us.

다음 글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: The Characteristics and Functions of Pourquoi Tales
Pourquoi Tales: Inventive Explanations for Animal Features
From Imaginative Tales to Scientific Explanations of Nature
How Animals Adapt Their Appearance to Changing Environments
The Requirement of Readers’ Imaginative Engagement in Pourquoi Tales

Right now, you are standing at the entrance of our first destination, Park Güell, (A)[designed / was designed] by Antoni Gaudi. It also lacked water because it was on a slope. However, Gaudi was able to build systems to collect and store water. 위 담화의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

(B) 동사 let은 ‘let+목적어+목적격보어(동사원형)’의 5형식 구문으로 쓰이므로 동사 let의 목적격보어 자리에 동사원형 look이 적절하다.
(C) 완전한 절(it ~ water)을 이끌어 동사 believed의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로 명사절 접속사 that이 적절하다.

body:
The tallest man in recorded history was 272 cm tall, but have you ever wondered what would happen if humans could grow to enormous sizes like the giant in Jack and the Beanstalk? Unfortunately, the answer to this hypothetical question is (A)[what / that] it is impossible due to the scale effect. When the length of an object doubles, its area increases by a factor of four (2x2), and its volume by a factor of eight (2x2x2). These changes can create many problems that would put the giant’s life in danger.
One issue is that the giant would not be able to stand properly on his own because of the weight pushing down on his feet. If a person’s height (B)[increases / increased] ten times, his weight would increase by a factor of 1,000 (10x10x10) because weight changes in proportion to volume. However, the area of the feet supporting his body would only increase by a factor of 100 (10x10). This means that his feet (C)[will / would] be under too much pressure to support the increased weight because the mass would have increased far more than the area of his feet.
윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: that / increases / will
what / increases / would
what / increased / would
that / increased / will
that / increased / would
solution:
(A) 완전한 절(it ~ effect)을 이끌어 be동사 is에 이어지는 주격보어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로 명사절 접속사 that이 알맞다.
(B) 사람의 키가 10배가 되는 것은 현재 사실과 반대되는 상황 또는 실현 가능성이 희박한 상황이므로, 가정법 과거 ‘If+주어+과거동사 ~, 주어+조동사 과거형+동사원형 …’의 구조가 되어야 하므로, if절의 동사로 과거동사 increased가 알맞다.
(C) 그의 발이 증가된 무게를 지탱하느라 지나치게 많은 압력을 받을 것이라는 that절의 내용은 현재 사실과 반대되는 상황 또는 실현 가능성이 희박한 상황(무게가 1000배, 발의 면적이 100배가 되는 것)을 가정하고 있으므로, 가정을 나타내는 조동사 would가 알맞다.

Without the Moon, our day would no longer be 24 hours. The Moon’s gravity causes the Earth’s ocean to rise and fall. Since the ocean is moving and the Earth is also spinning, friction occurs between them. This friction leads to a decrease in the rotation rate of the planet. Without the Moon, however, the Earth’s rotation would not slow down, resulting in a change in the length of a day. According to some scientists, when the Earth first formed, there was no Moon and a day was only five hours long. This indicates that without the Moon, we would see the Sun rise every five hours.
Additionally, the absence of the Moon would completely change weather patterns on Earth. We experience the beauty of different seasons because the Earth is tilted on its axis. The axis of rotation of the Earth is tilted at an angle of 23.5 degrees, and the Moon’s gravity holds the Earth in place by stabilizing the tilt. However, ⓐif there is no Moon, the tilt could vary wildly between 0 and 85 degrees. Suppose the Earth were tilted at an angle of 60 degrees. The hemisphere of the Earth facing the Sun would receive much more energy from the sun than the other hemisphere. ⓑThis could bring about extreme shifts in weather patterns, potentially made summers hotter and winters colder. If this trend continued, the Earth would become uninhabitable.
윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: the effects of disruptions to Earth’s natural cycles
the surprising price of a world without the moon
the unexpected ways objects in space influence our planet
the importance of natural cycles in maintaining life on Earth
the potential consequences of changes in Earth’s environmental balance
solution:

3. What if the oxygen concentration in the atmosphere doubled?
Oxygen is a vital gas for life, making up 21 percent of the Earth’s atmosphere. It is essential for breathing and is also necessary to burn common fuels like wood and oil ⓐto generate heat and light. Undoubtedly, it is an indispensable element for organisms on Earth. Then, would ⓑit be better to have a higher concentration of oxygen in the atmosphere? What would happen if the oxygen concentration were to double?
While more oxygen may seem ⓒbeneficial, it could have unexpected consequences, especially for insects. Insects, such as bees and dragonflies, do not have lungs and instead take in air through external openings called spiracles. Although insects can survive without lungs, their spiracles are (A)______. Therefore, with the current oxygen concentration, insects cannot evolve to be larger than their current size. If they were bigger in size, oxygen would not be able to reach the deepest parts of their bodies. However, if the concentration of oxygen were to double, insects could grow in size as oxygen would be more readily available. This increase in insect size could have a significant influence on the ecological environment, potentially ⓓdisrupting the food chain. Dragonflies, for example, may become ⓔas largely as eagles, altering the balance of predators and prey in the ecosystem.
Fortunately, you wouldn’t need to worry about giant insects chasing after you if this were to occur. If the oxygen concentration were to double, you would be able to run faster than you can right now. Considering that oxygen is used to break down energy so that muscles can use it, the increase in oxygen would help to use energy more efficiently and improve our capability for physical exercise. This leads us to expect that athletes would set new world records at the Olympics.
While these three thought experiments offer interesting possibilities, it is important to consider that they are simply based on imagination and have not been tested through scientific research.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓔ as largely as → as large as (‘~만큼 …한’의 의미를 갖는 원급 비교 'as+형용사/부사의 원급+as'의 구조가 쓰였으며, 동사 become의 보어가 as 사이에 들어가야 하므로, 부사 largely를 형용사 large로 고친다.)
